Hi Mike,

Order Shop···· (NerdOctaxe 12TH + NerdQX 8TH) was delivered Oct 8, 2026 to (address hidden), Italy (UPS (number hidden)). The B.144 SW-1202500 power supply that came with the NerdOctaxe failed on Oct 10. Label: 12V 25A, XT60 output.

The NerdOctaxe is running on the NerdQX's PSU for now, so the NerdQX is offline. I believe the 3-Month RMA with this order should cover the failure. Please send a replacement PSU from your EU stock, or tell me the next steps. I can ship the dead unit back on your prepaid EU label, and I sent photos of the label and connector.

Thanks,
Emilio V.
Handed to the team · Mailed part needed: replacement 12V 25A XT60 power supply from EU stock for a Ne

Hi Emilio,

Thanks for the detail, that makes the diagnosis easy. The important part first: the NerdOctaxe itself is fine. It boots and hashes on the NerdQX brick, which tells us the fault is in the power supply alone, not in the miner board. Nothing has to go back for the unit to be fixed, so there is no need to take the Octaxe apart or run any further tests on it.

On the power supply, the Bit144 SW-1202500 is a plain 12V 25A (300W) brick with an XT60 output, and that is all the NerdOctaxe asks for. Any decent 12V supply rated 20A or more with an XT60 lead will run it, with the XT60 keyed the usual way so you cannot reverse polarity. If you want both miners hashing again before a new brick reaches you, that is the quickest route locally. What I would avoid is leaving the Octaxe on the NerdQX brick for long: the QX supply is sized for the smaller board, and a 12TH Octaxe at stock voltage will sit near or above its limit, which tends to cause voltage sag, resets and eventually a second dead supply. If you do keep that setup running for a few days, drop the Octaxe's frequency and core voltage a step or two in the web UI so it draws well under the brick's rating. Please do not open either supply or cut and rejoin any leads.

One housekeeping note: the photos of the label and the connector did not come through on my side, so they have not been lost on you, they simply did not attach. The label figures you typed out are enough for me, so there is nothing you need to resend unless the team asks.

I have logged my findings as a power supply failure with a replacement brick from EU stock as the next step, and passed it to my colleagues who handle warranty shipments. They are offline over the weekend and pick it up Monday at 10am ET, and their answer, including whether they want the dead brick back and on what label, comes to you by email in this thread. If you want a second pair of eyes on the setup in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi Hal,

Following up on this. You said the warranty team would pick it up Monday and reply here, and I haven't heard anything yet. Can you confirm the replacement brick is shipping from EU stock, send me tracking once it goes out, and let me know whether you want the dead Bit144 back and what label to use?

Thanks,
Emilio
